summary: The constraints that decide whether a req is applicable — visa sponsorship, relocation support, language requirements — exist only as prose inside the HTML description and qualification fields, so this CLI must offer a client-side text filter over those fields with HTML stripped before matching.
reason:
amazon.jobs exposes no facet for any of these, and the fields are HTML fragments, so a pattern spanning a
or wrapped in tags misses against the raw text. The filter also has to tolerate ordinary prose containing regex metacharacters ("C++") rather than rejecting it as a bad pattern, and it needs a negation form because excluding a disqualifier is as common as searching for one. Matches are rare — sponsorship language appears in roughly 16 of 1000 reqs and relocation language in about 2 — so the scan-cap note that reports how many rows were examined is part of the feature, not decoration.
validated_outcome: Live `find --country SGP --description-contains "without sponsorship"` isolates the sponsorship-restricted req from 158 hits; the negated form returns the complement.
